segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Good afternoon. Can I help you?

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: Good afternoon. Yes, I've just transferred to the School of Education, and I'd like information about joining the library.

segments.speaker: LIBRARIA N
segments.en: Well, the School of Education has libraries on two sites, as I'm sure you know. This one here is the Fordham Site, and the other is on Castle Road.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: And is there any difference between the two libraries?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Not in terms of their facilities. Access to online databases and the Internet is available at both sites and each site has a range of reference materials on education.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: Oh yes. I see.

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: But the Castle Road site has books on the sociology of. education and a collection of textbooks and teaching resources covering most of the subjects taught in secondary schools.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: Ah, right, but I'm training to be a primary teacher so I need to look at materials for the five to eleven age group.

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Then you've come to the right place. At Fordham we hold material relating to primary education, as well as special needs, but of course you'll need to familiarise yourself with both sites to make the most of our resources.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: You haven't mentioned periodicals. Are they held at both sites?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Current issues, yes but if you want to look at back issues you'll need to use the CD-ROM databases which are held here at Ford ham.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: I see. Now, about borrowing books. I'm living out of town, so I'm hoping I can borrow quite a few items, and cut down on the number of trips I have to make . .

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Right, well, members can borrow two books at a time from each site.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: Only two books?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Only two from each site, but that's four altogether.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: Oh I see, and now long can I hang on to them for?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: The borrowing period is one month, but of course books can be renewed. You can renew any item a maximum of three times.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: Do I have to come to the library to do that?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: No, you can do it by telephone or email, but you can't renew overdue books this way, only before or on the due date stamped in the book. We'll need your full name, your borrower number and the name of the site library you borrowed the items from.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: So theoretically I can borrow books for up to three months- is that what you're saying?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Yes, provided they're not recalled.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: So, what happens then? •·

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Well, sometimes an item is requested by another borrower, in which case we'd send you a letter, and you'd have to return the book within seven working days. Don't forget we're closed o~ Sundays.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: I expect it'll take me a while to find what I need. There's such a lot here.

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Yes there is, but if you need help getting started, this term we're running three study skills workshops.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: Oh? What are they on?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Er, let me see. The first one's on resources- yes, here it is. How to use the library's resources. That includes everything. not · /29/30 just the print and technical resources.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: That sounds useful. Is there anything on using the Internet?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Er, let's see. The one on the Internet for beginners was last term. This /29/30 ·term it's finding research materials online. STUD~T : That sounds interesting too, hm, what's the last one?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: It's a workshop on dissertations. /29/30

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: What do you mean - how to write one?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: ErJlQ it's more to do with academic writing conventions, you know- writing a bibliography and how to refer to sources in your text. That sort of thing. Anyway, here's a leaflet with information about all three.

segments.speaker: STUDENT
segments.en: Thanks a lot. That'll be very useful.

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: You're welcome.
